decisions.title: Go for agent and relay core
decisions.decision: Use Go for the device agent and relay-server core.
decisions.rationale: Single-binary cross-platform distribution, straightforward concurrency, and a small runtime dependency surface.

decisions.title: Structured capabilities before raw shell
decisions.decision: Structured capabilities are the default execution interface; raw shell is denied by default.
decisions.rationale: Reduce prompt-injection blast radius and keep local policy explicit.

decisions.title: Outbound-only device networking
decisions.decision: Normal device connectivity originates outbound from the user PC.
decisions.rationale: Avoid exposing inbound services on user machines and work across NAT and firewalls.

decisions.title: Go 1.24 minimum for traversal-resistant filesystem execution
decisions.decision: Raise the project minimum to Go 1.24 and use os.Root for filesystem executor operations.
decisions.rationale: The project is new and security-sensitive; os.Root provides traversal-resistant operations without a check-then-use authorization race.

decisions.title: Remote payload cannot grant privileged approval
decisions.decision: CapabilityRequest contains no trusted approval boolean or token in Phase 1; privileged capabilities stop at APPROVAL_REQUIRED.
decisions.rationale: An LLM or compromised relay must not self-authorize mutation process execution or network clone.

decisions.title: Terminal-first Phase 4 control surface
decisions.decision: Close Phase 4 on the secure runnable outbound agent plus max-chat terminal client; move graphical multi-device chat UI/device selector to Phase 5.
decisions.rationale: The terminal surface proves the cryptographic controller/provider/tool path with a smaller attack surface and no new web auth/session layer. Graphical multi-device UI remains explicitly unproven rather than being conflated with source-complete terminal control.

decisions.title: Encrypted single-node relay snapshot with ephemeral bearer sessions
decisions.decision: Persist restart-critical relay trust command result and replay state in one bounded AES-256-GCM snapshot keyed by an external 32-byte secret; do not persist bearer sessions leases pairing offers or pairing receipts.
decisions.rationale: The self-hosted relay is currently single-node. A transactional encrypted snapshot is the smallest dependency-free durability mechanism, preserves replay protection across restart, avoids extending bearer-token authority across restart, and keeps a future database migration possible without changing protocol semantics.

decisions.title: Protocol-v1 fixtures are the cross-client compatibility boundary
decisions.decision: Future Cloudflare relay, MCP gateway, and other language/client adapters must conform to the published protocol-v1 canonical signing and restart vectors; they must not weaken device, generation, expiry, replay, or agent-session binding to gain compatibility.
decisions.rationale: A single executable language-neutral compatibility boundary prevents transport or adapter implementations from duplicating or drifting away from the security semantics already proven in the Go core.

decisions.title: Hybrid outbound WebSocket command transport with durable HTTPS result acknowledgement
decisions.decision: Use authenticated outbound WebSocket as the default agent command-delivery transport, retain long-poll as an explicit fallback, and keep device-session creation plus result submission on HTTPS so existing durable result acknowledgement semantics remain unchanged.
decisions.rationale: This removes constant polling and prepares the agent for Cloudflare WebSocket/Hibernation without changing protocol-v1 command authority, local policy, or the already-proven persistence boundary. Keeping results on HTTPS avoids introducing a second durability acknowledgement protocol in P6.

decisions.title: Adopt latest synchronized roadmap governance
decisions.decision: Pin Skill_Workflow c1d7e58a0fcadc606c8cf75c6283a17278f99259, make .workflow/roadmap.json the roadmap authority, generate docs/ROADMAP.md deterministically, and vendor the latest project-local governance tool pack while retaining the repo-specific Go-aware sequence extractor as a documented extension.
decisions.rationale: The latest workflow makes roadmap/state synchronization blocking and provides project-local deterministic tools. Replacing the Go-aware extractor with the generic upstream extractor would regress Go sequence coverage, so the project keeps that extension while adopting the latest contract and LF determinism.

decisions.title: Cloudflare relay is a thin per-device Durable Object adapter
decisions.decision: Implement P7 as a TypeScript Cloudflare Worker that routes each device to one SQLite-backed Durable Object; use the Hibernation WebSocket API for the outbound agent connection and preserve protocol-v1 cryptographic/session authority rather than creating Cloudflare-specific command authority.
decisions.rationale: Cloudflare recommends SQLite-backed Durable Objects for new namespaces and Hibernation for WebSocket servers. A per-device object gives serialized strongly-consistent state and keeps Cloudflare-specific transport/storage code behind the already accepted protocol-v1 compatibility boundary.
